summary: January 2026 paper proposing Episodic Context Reconstruction — retrieving prior episode summaries instead of preprocessing memory at ingestion time. Improves retrieval relevance by deferring semantic compression until query time.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — relevant to cross-run episodic memory, but this capability is already tracked by open issue HID-188 (feat(agents): inject cross-run episodic memory into planner and executor prompts).

summary: Agent that edits its own code and iterates using a meta-agent chosen from an archive. Reports 17-53% gains on SWE Bench Verified. Uses archive selection to propagate successful strategies.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — theme of plan repair and adversarial critique is already covered by HID-93 and HID-186. The self-editing of agent code/prompts is out of scope for AgentForge (agents are CLI subprocesses, not editable at runtime).

summary: March 2026 paper training reflection/self-correction into model weights via RL, reducing inference-time compute overhead ~40%. Three-step loop: initial generation, bug-aware reflection, self-correction.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — requires model fine-tuning/RL training. AgentForge orchestrates existing CLI models and cannot retrain them. Out of scope architecturally.

summary: LangGraph v1.2 (May 2026) reportedly added a DeltaChannel feature; details unconfirmed from primary sources. Thread-scoped checkpointing is well-established; cross-session memory still requires external add-on layers.

summary: MemAlign stores episodic interactions, distills them into semantic rules, and retrieves rules at inference. Proposes a 'write path' as a first-class memory concern alongside retrieval.
